correctness.rationale: The proof verifies p[2j]=0 and p[2j+1]=1-p[j], excludes 11 and 0000, forces all ones in any factor to share parity, excludes odd n>=5 by rotation parity and runs, and explicitly proves that delta induces a bijection between length-m and length-2m Lie classes for every m>=2. The three base values each equal two. The derived formula follows for every n>=1 by halving. Executed verify.py checks both word constructions, equality of factor sets between prefixes of lengths 8192 and 16384, full class counts for 1<=n<=200, and the class-bijection identity for all tested even n. Finite tests corroborate but do not establish the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full-conjugacy invariant is defined by Bell and Shallit (2021), but their explicit examples omit period doubling. The original 2014 period-doubling cyclic-complexity result uses existence of one representative, and Currie (2023) supplies the parity/desubstitution prerequisite without the new full Lie-class bijection or all-length support formula. Direct published-source comparisons and published-finding corpus semantic searches found no theorem with the same conclusion. The possibility of unindexed equivalent work is retained as residual risk.
residual_risks: A hidden lemma in another work on automatic sequences or Toeplitz factors might be equivalent to the length-halving Lie recurrence without being indexed by the search terms.
Currie’s desubstitution results and Cassaigne’s cyclic count are related enough that the specialization could have been observed informally; no such stated full classification was found.
Semantic search alone does not prove global uniqueness or publication priority.

value.rationale: This is an all-length explicit instance of the Lie complexity introduced in 2021 for a canonical aperiodic non-Sturmian automatic word. The proof uncovers an exact substitution-based conjugacy-class bijection, two geometric progressions supporting every nonzero count, and zero-density support. It gives a mathematically motivated classification beyond a table or routine parameter substitution, and distinguishes the stronger universal-rotation statistic from previously available cyclic complexity.
